Depth of discussion of concurrency concepts [LO3-PO6]

scores.justification: The assumptions and additional requirements are listed only as brief single-line table entries (e.g., "A ground slot is held from landing clearance until take-off ends") and asserted bullet points ("flight-adaptive self-escalating holding pattern") without detailed architectural prose. However, all eight assumptions in Table 1 are directly mapped to concrete Java implementation mechanisms.

scores.criterion: Explanation of the safety aspects of multi-threaded system implemented [LO3-PO6]
scores.justification: The safety analysis in Section 2.3 relies entirely on a concise summary table rather than an in-depth discussion of thread interactions and edge cases. Nonetheless, Table 2 accurately identifies key concurrency hazards—including race conditions, deadlock via Coffman conditions, starvation, and memory visibility—and maps each to the exact mechanism protecting it.

The justifications in Table 3 are compressed into one-line phrases (e.g., "Wait for N events without thread references" vs "join() needs handles") rather than thorough comparative evaluations. Still, the report provides working code snippets for all major primitives and explicitly contrasts each chosen java.util.concurrent facility against a rejected alternative.

scores.criterion: Depth of discussion of concurrency concepts [LO3-PO6]
scores.justification: The conceptual discussions in Sections 2.2 and 3.2 are very brief (2–3 sentences per concept) and some prose in Section 3.2 confuses the refuelling truck's BlockingQueue with the ATC's pickNext() priority logic. Despite this brevity, the report covers a wide range of concurrency concepts (mutual exclusion, CAS, condition synchronisation, latches, producer-consumer) and backs them with verifiable simulation logs.
